judged_text: For dynamic collective bookings (no eventTypeId), users are loaded from the request-supplied dynamicUserList and each listed user's destinationCalendar is pushed into teamDestinationCalendars, which then drives per-destination event creation using those users' credentials via the new unscoped DB credential fetch. A booker can compose a dynamic collective link naming arbitrary usernames and, by picking a slot where those users are free, cause calendar events (with the booker-controlled booking title) to be written into arbitrary users' personal calendars using their OAuth credentials — cross-user calendar writes driven by client-supplied input rather than by the event type owner.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking`, when `!eventTypeId`, `loadUsers` fetches arbitrary users by `username: { in: dynamicUserList }` (request-driven list) with no diff-visible authorization/ownership binding to the event type (`prisma.user.findMany({ where: { username: { in: dynamicUserList }}})`). For collective team events, it then pushes each loaded user’s `destinationCalendar` into `teamDestinationCalendars` and appends them onto `evt.destinationCalendar` (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). Separately, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates `event.destinationCalendar` and, when a `DestinationCalendar` has a `credentialId`, will fetch that credential directly from DB by id (`prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId }})`) and call `createEvent` with it. This combination makes it feasible (based on the diff) for client-supplied usernames to influence which users’ destination calendars/credentials are used for calendar writes, enabling cross-user calendar event creation without a shown authorization check.
